title: Functional analysis
stage: Graduate study and qualifying exams in mathematics
audience: a graduate student in the first years of a mathematics PhD preparing for qualifying exams, or a graduate preparing to apply for one
purpose: Learn analysis in infinite-dimensional spaces: normed and Banach spaces, bounded operators and dual spaces, Hilbert spaces, orthonormal bases and Fourier series, the Riesz representation theorem, the Hahn–Banach theorem, the Baire category theorem and its consequences (uniform boundedness, open mapping and closed graph theorems), weak convergence in outline, compact operators, the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators, and applications to integral and differential equations.
primary_reading: Measure, Integration & Real Analysis by Sheldon Axler (free, open access)

weeks.2: Bounded linear operators and dual spaces
weeks.7: The Baire category theorem and the uniform boundedness principle
weeks.8: The open mapping and closed graph theorems
weeks.9: Weak convergence and reflexivity in outline
weeks.11: The spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators
weeks.12: Applications to integral and differential equations

blocks.deliverable: Prove that supplied spaces are complete and compute operator norms.
Expand a supplied function in an orthonormal basis and verify Parseval's identity.
Use the Hahn–Banach theorem to separate a point from a closed subspace.
Week 7 midterm; apply the uniform boundedness principle to a supplied family of operators.
Prove that a supplied integral operator is compact.
Solve a supplied integral equation with the spectral theorem.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Qualifying-exam dossier in functional analysis: write complete solutions to twenty exam-style problems, prove the Hahn–Banach, uniform boundedness and open mapping theorems in full, approximate the eigenvalues of a compact integral operator in plain Python by discretization and compare them with the exact values, and write a two-page summary of the main theorems with their hypotheses.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
